title: How AI agents shape experts’ judgment calls
finding: Analysts followed assigned agent preferences in a bounded analytical task.
limits: Strengthened preferences; choices could be defensible; no long-term capability result.
decision: Test independent judgment and justified reliance.

title: The Customer Never Sees the Goal
finding: Hidden goals produced vulnerability-targeted replies in synthetic tasks.
limits: Model replies, not measured customer persuasion or harm.
decision: Inspect configured objectives and test matched disclosures.

title: Just the Facts
finding: Factual arguments supported belief correction in two online experiments.
limits: Specific U.S. conspiracy-belief setting; no universal autonomy result.
decision: Include beneficial factual correction as contrary evidence.

title: AI-Assisted Classification under Correlation Neglect and Trust
finding: Shared evidence and trust affect how assistance changes decisions.
limits: Specific classification tasks; no long-term skill result.
decision: Measure evidence overlap and appropriate reliance separately.

title: Provenance-Aware Belief Updating in Human-AI Feedback Loops
limits: Supplied lineage, limited models and controlled tasks.
decision: Group derivative reports by originating observation.

title: Upstream Influence, Downstream Re-Anchoring in LLM Agent Chains
finding: Source access and handoffs affected influence; some downstream re-anchoring occurred.
limits: Bounded case set; no human agency measurement.
decision: Preserve source exposure and test influence beyond final explanations.

title: Context Is a Pipeline, Not a Window
finding: Truncation lost evidence and increased work in an agent task.
limits: Accuracy causation unresolved; human effects not measured.
decision: Expose omissions and verify delivery before consequential review.
